transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-22
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel; Jordan Lee; Kiran Das; Alex Chen; Priya Sharma; Diego Ramos; Sara Lin

Auto-generated summary: Walkthrough of Redwood Optimize suggestions for caching and batching. Emphasis on runtime cache "lookahead" (prefix warming) and burst-capacity presets.

[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone thanks for taking the time, i'm maya from Redwood, i'll kick us off. uh quick intro, jordan our se will jump into the console and the cost workbook after a quick context check.
[00:22] Alex Chen: thanks maya, yeah i got the invite. we're trying to understand how to reduce per-api cost for our chat flows without blowing up tail latency, and also curious about dedicated vs hosted burst options.
[00:38] Jordan Lee: yeah great, alex. quick gate - can you confirm load shape, like do you have long sessions or short interactions? that drives cache hit rates.
[00:47] Priya Sharma: most sessions are short — avg 4 turns, but we have spikes during campaigns where concurrency goes x10 for 20 mins. prompts are typically 80–220 tokens, so kv cache helps but need to know warm-up strategy.
[01:12] Jordan Lee: perfect, so two knobs we'll focus on: micro-batching heuristics (we call them micro-batches to avoid increasing latency) and lookahead prefix warming — that's a lightweight KV prefetch that reduces repeated encoder cost.
[01:30] Diego Ramos: how stateful is that prefetch? is it per user session or shared? our infra team is worried about memory pressure on the gpu.
[01:41] Kiran Das: good q — the typical approach is session-affine keys with TTLs. you can choose per-session cache or shared prefixes. shared prefixes reduce memory but lower hit for unique contexts. the Console exposes an estimated memory footprint per cache config.
[02:03] Maya Patel: i'll show the Console view — it's in Optimize -> Cache Profiles. jordan would you pull up the workbook?
[02:11] Jordan Lee: sure, pulling it now. bear with me — okay loading Cost Model v2. so first slide, baseline: no caching, naive batching of 1, unit cost is X tokens. then we simulate two scenarios: 1) micro-batching at 20ms window and 2) 100ms window with prefix warming.
[03:02] [Jordan shares screens — link posted in chat: https://redwood.app/share/abc123] 
[03:15] Priya Sharma: can you explain micro-batching 20ms vs 100ms in practical terms? how will that affect our P99?
[03:26] Jordan Lee: yes. 20ms windows aggregate a few concurrent requests so you get batching benefits with minimal added latency; 100ms gets higher batch sizes which lowers cost-per-token but can add 70–120ms median for cold paths, and tail depends on traffic shape. For your campaign spikes, 100ms may be acceptable if you have burst capacity and can tolerate an SLO shift to 250ms P99.
[03:58] Alex Chen: i see. what about the KV / prefix cache hit rate numbers — can you show the hit curve?
[04:06] Jordan Lee: yep — here's the simulated hit curve based on your reported session shape. with per-session prefix warming and TTL 30 minutes, we get ~62% hit rate on decoder KV reuse for similar prompts. with shared prefixes TTL 60 minutes, hit goes up to 78% but per-gpu memory usage increases by 1.8x.
[04:36] Sara Lin: 1.8x memory — is that for our projected 2000 concurrent users?
[04:42] Jordan Lee: that's based on the sample dataset you gave us earlier scaled to 2k conc. real numbers vary — this is why we want the actual session heatmap.
[04:53] Priya Sharma: are there ways to compress KV to keep memory down? like quantized storage?
[04:59] Jordan Lee: yes — we support block quantization for KV storage which reduces memory by ~2.6x with minor accuracy drop for most models. we can also evict based on LRU or score-based eviction. the Console shows the expected accuracy delta in the optimize panel.
[05:20] Diego Ramos: security question — where are cached keys stored for Redwood Private? encrypted at rest?
[05:26] Maya Patel: yes, for Private deployments KV is within your VPC and you can integrate with customer KMS; keys are encrypted, access controlled via RBAC, and audit logs are available. we'll share SOC2 docs and the audit-log samples.
[05:46] Alex Chen: great. ok, show me the cost delta — i want to see best-case and worst-case.
[05:51] Jordan Lee: slide — cost sim. baseline cost per 1M queries: $X. micro-batch 20ms + per-session cache = 32% cost reduction. 100ms + shared cache + quantized KV = 61% reduction but P95 increases slightly. details in workbook.
[06:22] Maya Patel: quick interjection — we also recommend routing policies during spikes: route to cheaper model variants or to dedicated burst nodes to keep latency. that gives another 10–20% saving depending on model choices.
[06:37] Priya Sharma: model variants — so we'd have a smaller model for fallbacks? how does that affect UI quality?
[06:44] Kiran Das: yes, you can have top-line model PD-2 for most traffic and fallback to PD-1 for heavy burst. Redwood Optimize's evals can estimate quality delta across your prompt set; you can set automatic fallback thresholds in Console.
[07:05] Alex Chen: ok. can you run the 10k sim with our exact prompt distribution?
[07:10] Jordan Lee: yes, that's the plan — we'll run on sandbox with your distribution after you send the CSV. we'll send a transcript of the run plus the raw logs.
[07:18] Priya Sharma: what's the recommended TTL for prefix warming? 30 vs 60 — sounds like tradeoff between memory and hit rate.
[07:26] Jordan Lee: based on your cadence, 30 min looks like sweet spot; during campaigns you can flip to 60 with a shorter eviction policy for less-used keys. We can automate TTL changes based on traffic via Console policies.
[07:45] [12:00] Jordan Lee: apologies i'm jumping ahead — showing the runtime memory estimate panel. note redwood's estimate is conservative by ~10% to avoid OOMs.
[12:18] Diego Ramos: does Dedicated give us a guaranteed memory footprint per GPU?
[12:24] Maya Patel: yes, Dedicated reserves the pool and we can provide an SLA for memory availability and throughput. Dedicated + burst nodes gives you the isolation you want for campaigns.
[12:39] [18:30] Alex Chen: procurement question — we need audit logs and SSO details for our legal team, and we need an SLA that covers both uptime and tail latency for peak windows.
[18:45] Maya Patel: we have enterprise packs — we'll attach SOC2 and SAML docs. For tail latency we can commit to region-level P95 with penalties — we'll follow up with a draft SLA.
[19:05] Priya Sharma: curious about warm start vs cold start when you rotate model versions — do you pre-warm caches?
[19:14] Kiran Das: yes, Console supports staged rollouts and pre-warm scripts — we can pre-populate KV for top N prefixes during rollout to avoid cold starts. that's in the rollout plan section.
[19:36] [26:00] Jordan Lee: running through the benchmark plan: 10k-sessions synthetic run, vary concurrency to emulate campaign, collect P50/P95/P99 and batch size distribution. we'll also capture per-token cost and per-request cost.
[26:22] Priya Sharma: can you also include a run where we simulate misaligned sessions — i.e., lots of unique prompts that reduce cache hits — to see worst-case?
[26:32] Jordan Lee: absolutely — we'll run best/mid/worst case.
[26:40] Alex Chen: what's the onboarding time for Private vs Dedicated? we might need Private for compliance but want the fastest path.
[26:49] Maya Patel: hosted API is fastest (minutes to get keys), Dedicated is days to weeks depending on pool size, Private (VPC) is 4–8 weeks typically for on-prem-like setups plus security reviews.
[27:06] Diego Ramos: hmm, 4-8 weeks — ok we'll evaluate Dedicated for short term.
[27:12] Sara Lin: pricing model for Dedicated — is that reserved monthly?
[27:17] Maya Patel: yes, reserved capacity with optional burst credits. we'll send a sample reserved quote.
[27:26] [34:00] Jordan Lee: showing optimized config suggestions in Console: Profile A (low-latency): 20ms micro-batch, per-session prefix TTL 30m, quantized KV off. Profile B (cost-optimized): 100ms micro-batch, shared prefix TTL 60m, quantized KV on, fallback model PD-1 for >150qps bursts.
[34:32] Priya Sharma: what's the expected quality loss with PD-1 fallback? 0.5–2%?
[34:38] Kiran Das: for your retail prompts, evals show ~1.1% drop in NLU accuracy on the sample set, mostly in multi-step reasoning. We'll include eval traces in the workbook.
[35:00] Alex Chen: show me the Console policy UI for automating TTL changes.
[35:08] Jordan Lee: here — you can create a policy: when concurrency > X and average latency < Y, switch to Profile B; else revert. triggers can be time-based or metric-based.
[35:31] Diego Ramos: and is that rollback automatic if latency climbs?
[35:36] Jordan Lee: yes you can set automatic fallbacks tied to latency SLOs. it'll route to a safe model or reduce batch windows.
[35:46] [41:00] Maya Patel: ok final recap — action items: we'll run the 10k sims (best/mid/worst), send the Cost Model v2 and sample reserved quote, and provide SOC2 + SSO docs. Starlit to send session heatmap CSV. we'll aim for a pilot kickoff in two weeks.
[41:24] Alex Chen: sounds good. a couple of smaller things — can you annotate the workbook with the exact batch/window assumptions so our infra ppl can reproduce?
[41:31] Jordan Lee: yes i'll annotate and include the exact benchmark script and seeds.
[41:38] Priya Sharma: thanks — appreciate the thoroughness.
[41:45] Maya Patel: thanks everyone. one last note: i'll include a quick video note on how to interpret the P99 numbers in the workbook.
[41:55] Alex Chen: great, bye all.
